results.fact: Whether the Northwest Couloir is the standard descent after climbing the Northeast Buttress
results.correct_value: The Southwest Face / south side is the usual descent; the Northwest Couloir is an occasional alternative.
results.evidence: The Mountaineers Southwest Face page gives the descent as a double-rope rappel from the top of the last pitch then downclimbing the climbing route, and suggests the northwest chimney downclimb only as an alternative. A CascadeClimbers Northeast Buttress report descends the south side, noting its heavier traffic. A WTA trip report describes a Northwest Couloir descent as longer but workable. So the couloir is an alternative descent, not the standard one.

results.fact: Hardest pitch grade / crux grade disagreement
results.evidence: The published grade is 5.2 (PG13); the same description gives pitch 1 as 5.1-5.6 depending on which side of the chimney you start, and another description rates a short left-trending break through the overhanging band at about 5.5. These are variant-dependent moves under a stated route grade, reproduced faithfully; rock_grade and beta name the 5.5 band. No two sources support a different headline grade.

results.fact: Ice grade (route-level ice_grade vs crux pitch grades)
results.evidence: Mountain Project grades the route AI2 steep snow (P1 70-degree ice, P4 50-70 degree snow and ice). The Mountaineers list it as a Grade II ice climb and a trip report puts it around AI2+. The row's own schedule also says Grade II ice. The AI3 labels on P1 and P4 are the outliers.
